text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Italy ranks first on the list of foreign investors in Romania.
- The Romanian Oil Company will be dissolved on July 1 and replaced with a new firm grouping three refineries, a petroleum products retailer and an oil transport company.
- The Banca Agricola bank gave the farming sectors credits worth 195 billion lei, needed to complete seasonal works.
- Police investigations show that some 380 private firms are operating in Romania without being legally registered.
- The transport ministry will launch Romania's first private train on June 1.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The tranport ministry will go ahead with plans to suspend the licences of the shipping firms which failed to pay their employees in time, the paper says.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The SNCFR railway authority will complete its restructuring programme by next January, the paper says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- U.S. President Bill Clinton hailed in a letter addressed to Romanian President Emil Constantinescu the "historic" meeting between Constantinescu and his Hungarian counterpart Arpad Goncz. The Romanian-Hungarian reconciliation could serve as a model to Europe and the entire world, Clinton said.
- Hungary's vital interests are linked to Romania's quick admission into NATO, Goncz said in a speach to Romania's parliament.
- Romania and Slovenia have increased their chances to be invited to join NATO in a first wave of the alliance's expansion, the paper says.
- Romania and Hungary signed an accord on rapid notification in case of nuclear accidents.
ADEVARUL
- Hungary will open a consulate in the Transylvanian city of Cluj on June 1, under a basic treaty signed with Romania last year.
- The government will subsidise electricity and gas prices for household consumption, Industry Minister Calin Popescu Tariceanu said.

- The former ruling leftist Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) will lodge a no-confidence vote this week slamming the government for failing to keep electoral promises, PDSR president Ion Iliescu told a news conference.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romanian children start to drink alcohol at the age of 12, while at the age of 17 some 87 percent of them drink regularly, a survey showed. ($ = 7,081 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
